numerical_failure.observed_behavior: For GroupBy.quantile groups containing a non-null NaN value that is not flagged by the null mask (e.g. a non-null NaN in a pyarrow/masked float array), the quickselect buffer corruption yields non-monotonic incorrect numerical results. For all-NaT datetime-like groups, the result comes back as NaN, gets cast to int64 (i8), and on some platforms this becomes 0 (Unix epoch), i.e. all-NaT becomes 1970-01-01 instead of iNaT.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Non-null NaNs that are not flagged by the mask must be treated as NA and skipped during the quickselect kth_smallest_c ordering comparisons, matching the non-grouped Series.quantile result. For all-NaT datetime-like groups, NaN placeholders should be mapped to iNaT explicitly so all-NaT groups remain iNaT (instead of platform-dependent Unix epoch), also silencing an "invalid value encountered in cast" warning.
trigger_conditions: GroupBy.quantile quickselect rewrite (GH#64330): a group contains a non-null NaN value that is not flagged by the null mask (e.g. NaN from a pyarrow or masked float array where mask==0 for that NaN)
GroupBy.quantile on datetime-like data where a group is all-NaT
Platforms/architectures where casting NaN to i8 yields 0 instead of INT64_MIN (noted for arm64/Apple Silicon/Graviton)

oracle_clues: Oracle #1: non-null NaNs that are not flagged by the null mask must be treated as NA, matching the non-grouped Series.quantile result (stated in PR body).
Oracle #2: all-NaT datetime-like groups must map to iNaT explicitly instead of platform-dependent cast result (0 -> 1970-01-01 on arm64; INT64_MIN (== NaT) on x86).

category_specific_evidence: Special values involved are NaN and NaT.

NaN case: a float NaN that is not flagged by the null mask (a non-null NaN in a pyarrow or masked float array where mask==0 for that entry) must be treated as NA; otherwise it corrupts kth_smallest_c's ordering comparisons and yields non-monotonic results.

Where NaN enters (quickselect/counting): during group_quantile counting and copying into the quickselect buffer, the code filters using mask[start+j]==0; additionally, for float32_t or float64_t it must skip float values where values[start+k] != values[start+k] (the NaN check) so they are not copied into tmp and so comparisons remain valid.
NaN handling rule: in the loop, for numeric_t == float32_t or float64_t, if values[start + j] != values[start + j] then continue (treat that NaN like other NAs).

NaT case: all-NaT datetime-like groups came back as NaN and were cast to i8; the cast is platform dependent (INT64_MIN (== NaT) on x86 but 0 (Unix epoch) on arm64), so all-NaT groups silently became 1970-01-01 on Apple Silicon/Graviton.

Where NaT enters/what correct handling is: after quantile computation, the all-NaT positions produce NaN that is cast to i8; those positions must be mapped to iNaT explicitly to prevent platform-dependent epoch values and to silence an "invalid value encountered in cast" warning.
reproduction_risks: No evidence in the passages about +/-inf, signed zero, or subnormals; only NaN and NaT are explicitly covered.
No evidence in the passages about dtype differences beyond the float32_t/float64_t NaN check; dtype/precision/magnitude regime/tolerance are otherwise not stated explicitly for the failing scenarios.

provenance.value: For GroupBy.quantile groups containing a non-null NaN value that is not flagged by the null mask (e.g. a non-null NaN in a pyarrow/masked float array), the quickselect buffer corruption yields non-monotonic incorrect numerical results. For all-NaT datetime-like groups, the result comes back as NaN, gets cast to int64 (i8), and on some platforms this becomes 0 (Unix epoch), i.e. all-NaT becomes 1970-01-01 instead of iNaT.

Non-null NaNs that are not flagged by the mask must be treated as NA and skipped during the quickselect kth_smallest_c ordering comparisons, matching the non-grouped Series.quantile result. For all-NaT datetime-like groups, NaN placeholders should be mapped to iNaT explicitly so all-NaT groups remain iNaT (instead of platform-dependent Unix epoch), also silencing an "invalid value encountered in cast" warning.
